title: Cluster Lifecycle Map and Status Surface for Private Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design an at-a-glance and inspectable status surface for Private/VPC clusters that makes lifecycle state, networking health, ongoing upgrades, and rollback options immediately actionable for operators.

Scope: Two primary surfaces — 1) Fleet list compact tile (cluster cards) optimized for quick triage across tens of clusters; 2) Cluster detail lifecycle map: an interactive timeline + transition graph that shows provisioning, healthy, degraded, draining, upgrading, and decommissioned states with associated network and KMS health overlays.

Success criteria: 
- 80% of internal platform engineers can identify the current cluster state and whether network/KMS connectivity is the root cause within 30s in a usability session.
- Prototype includes handoff-ready specs (Figma + interaction notes) and a prioritized acceptance checklist for ENG implementation.
- Telemetry and event contract defined so Console can feed runtime alerts to the incident pipeline (SLOs + sample payloads).

Constraints and trade-offs: 
- Must avoid overloading the fleet list UI; compact tiles will surface only 3 primary signals (state, network latency class, upgrade in-progress boolean) with an action affordance to open the lifecycle map.
- Full lifecycle map will accept slightly higher visual complexity in exchange for deep troubleshooting tools (node groups, last successful snapshot, recent API errors).
- We will not build a full network topology animator in this iteration to keep delivery window tight; instead provide a network health overlay and a link to a separate topology viewer (ENG backlog).

Accessibility and localization: All status colors will have redundant labels and icons; timeline keyboard navigation and screen-reader announcement behavior are specified in the prototype notes. Copy will be localized (EN/FR/DE initial set).
comments: 2026-02-14 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff done with PM (Ravi) and ENG lead (Sofia). Captured primary use cases: triage during incidents, pre-upgrade health checks, and SLA reporting. Decided to split work into Fleet Tile + Detail Map. Created initial task list and research plan.

2026-02-18 — Liam Nguyen: Early sketches reviewed. Engineering raised concern about real-time socket load if we surface node-level telemetry in fleet view; agreed to limit fleet view to aggregated indicators and lazy-load detail map on demand.

2026-02-22 — Usability Session 1: 6 platform engineers. Findings: participants expected 'Upgrade' state to show both planned and in-progress upgrades; added a small timeline marker to indicate 'planned window' vs 'active'. Participants also requested one-click 'pause/rollback' flow (safeguarded by confirmation + RBAC check).

2026-02-26 — Design critique: PM asked for stronger emphasis on network root-cause detection. Updated detail map to include network zone overlay and last successful handshake timestamp. Created microcopy for 'Network degraded' CTA to run connectivity recheck.

2026-03-01 — Prototype iteration: Built interactive Figma prototype with keyboard timeline scrubbing, node group hover cards, and a compact 'incident snapshot' export. Shared with ENG for feasibility review (link in attachments).

2026-03-05 — Review notes from Sofia (ENG): Implementation complexity acceptable if we keep the fleet tile payload small and offload heavy telemetry to a lazy endpoint. ENG requested explicit API contract for lifecycle transitions and sample events; added to attachments and action items.

2026-03-05 — Liam Nguyen: Ready for design handoff. Open items: define telemetry schema (ENG), finalize microcopy for localized strings (i18n), and schedule 2 follow-up usability tests with SREs and an enterprise customer pilot.
